title: Telegram assistant emits duplicate and contradictory capture acknowledgements

rootCause.defect1: The CaptureRoute=true fallback drives two reply sinks: (A) NewBotCaptureFn -> Bot.handleTextCapture persists AND replies (replyWithMapping '. Saved …' / captureErrorReply '? Failed to save …'); (B) the renderer sends resp.Body 'saved as an idea — i'll surface it later.'. Two messages per turn.
rootCause.defect2: For a bare '/ask', StripShortcutPrefix('/ask') == '' so sink A's callCapture fails ('? Failed to save') while sink B still claims 'saved as an idea' — a false, contradictory pair; the renderer asserted the idea was saved even when it was not.

resolution: Silence the bot-side capture hook on the assistant path and make it report persistence honestly. CaptureFn now returns error; NewBotCaptureFn delegates to Bot.captureIdeaSilent (persist via shared persistTextIdea, NO reply; empty text -> assistant_adapter.ErrNothingToCapture; errDuplicate -> nil benign success). HandleUpdate inspects the returned error and, on failure, replaces the 'saved as an idea' response with an honest single line via honestCaptureFallbackFailure (nothing-to-save prompt vs generic failure), rendered through the default StatusAnswered body path (single message). The legacy plain-text handleTextCapture keeps its own '. Saved …' reply (BS-001 UX preserved). Four adversarial regression tests added; all GREEN; go test ./... (compile+vet, filtered) clean; both changed packages ok.

Stability/operations review of the three production files this packet changed (internal/telegram/bot.go, internal/telegram/assistant_wiring.go, internal/telegram/assistant_adapter/adapter.go) across four axes. No suite re-run: unit, full integration, targeted integration and e2e --go-package assistant were all measured earlier in this same session and re-running them would yield no new stability information. GOROUTINE/LIFECYCLE clean: the fix adds no goroutine, timer or background worker; the new branch in HandleUpdate sits between rootSpan (ended by defer, adapter.go:353-355) and renderSpan (ended on both branches, adapter.go:403 and :408) and opens no span, so it cannot leak one per turn. CONCURRENCY clean and structurally so: the ingresses are mutually exclusive (wiring.go:838-859 -- the webhook branch does not call Bot.Start), and webhook is the concurrent shape (net/http, one goroutine per request into the same safeHandleMessage), so the review assumed the stricter concurrent shape. The load-bearing property is that the fix REMOVES A REPLY SINK rather than adding a dedup flag, so there is no acknowledgement state for concurrent turns to race on; a stateful fix would have needed synchronisation. All Adapter fields the new code reads are write-once in NewAdapter (adapter.go:127-134) except assistant, which is RWMutex-guarded; resp is a local and honestCaptureFallbackFailure returns a fresh struct, copying Routing without mutating it. RESOURCE USAGE clean: request body truncated to maxShareTextLen, response bounded by io.LimitReader(maxAPIResponseBytes), duration bounded by both the request context and httpClient{Timeout:30s} (bot.go:182), no retries added. The truncation bound was nearly lost -- it used to live inside handleTextCapture and the fix moved it down into the shared persistTextIdea, so the new silent path inherits it. Redelivery is safe: errDuplicate (capture API 409) maps to nil, and the webhook handler returns 200 unconditionally for any well-formed authenticated update (webhook_handler.go:264), so a failed capture or render cannot provoke a Telegram retry. CONFIG clean: the fix introduces NO new configuration value (its two user-facing strings are compile-time constants); NewAdapter rejects nil Capture / MaxMessageChars<=0 / bad MarkdownMode as construction errors (adapter.go:146-158) and ASSISTANT_TRANSPORTS_TELEGRAM_MODE is mustString + closed-vocabulary validated (assistant.go:402, :576, :614). Verification: ./smackerel.sh lint exit 0 (sha256 e308658676d5853a2bcc5ec398b93e6180919541ed8a512a34b662535b879ba0, 157 lines) -- this is the surface that runs go vet, whose copylocks/loopclosure checks are the mechanical counterpart to the static concurrency reasoning. HONEST LIMIT: the RACE DETECTOR WAS NOT RUN. The repo CLI exposes no --race selector (smackerel.sh test surface, lines 58-62) and a bare 'go test -race' would violate terminal discipline, so the concurrency verdict is STATIC (field-mutability analysis + go vet) and is NOT a claim that a dynamic detector was clean. THREE OBSERVATIONS recorded, none a defect in this packet, none fixed inline: (1) webhook mode never closes b.done -- close(b.done) exists in exactly one place (bot.go:381, inside the long-poll goroutine that webhook mode deliberately never starts), so Bot.Stop always burns its 5s wait (bot.go:1562-1566) while the caller budgets 2s and ABANDONS it (runWithTimeout runs fn in a goroutine and proceeds without cancelling, shutdown.go:87-91, :159-183), leaving assembler.FlushAll/mediaAssembler.FlushAll racing process exit -- buffered captures can be lost on restart. Pre-existing since spec 061 SCOPE-05; latent, not currently biting, because this packet's own recorded deploy evidence reports the startup line 'telegram bot started' which is emitted only on the long_poll branch (wiring.go:851) -- read off the record, NOT verified against the running system this phase. (2) a failed capture is still counted outcome=captured: the facade emits FacadeTurnsTotal and the assistant_turn line from a defer inside Handle (facade.go:511-513, :559) with deriveFacadeOutcome returning OutcomeCaptured for CaptureRoute (facade.go:1891-1893), all BEFORE the adapter's capture hook runs (adapter.go:390); honestCaptureFallbackFailure sets StatusAnswered and leaves ErrorCause empty, so the metric never reflects a persist failure. This fix strictly IMPROVED the situation (before it CaptureFn had no error return at all; it added the error channel plus slog.Error at bot.go:821) without closing it -- prose is honest, structure is not yet. (3) local dev-stack drift, verified read-only and NOT repaired: smackerel-smackerel-core-1 restarts=569 exit=1 with networks=0 while postgres carries alias 'postgres' on smackerel_default; the app's response is CORRECT (fatal startup error at ERROR, exit 1, no silent DSN fallback). Nothing was restarted -- other suites may be using Docker. No DoD item checked, no uservalidation.md edit, no scopes.md edit, certification.certifiedCompletedPhases deliberately NOT written.

executionHistory.evidence: report.md#regression-phase. Verdict REGRESSION_FREE. The reclassification of this packet's regression coverage from e2e-api to integration introduced no failures anywhere; the assistant e2e package is green with zero failures. Three capture-path e2e tests SKIPPED on status="unavailable" with capture_route=false, which independently CONFIRMS the root cause measured during the test phase (provider unavailable => capture hook never fires); per BUG-061-008 the product is CORRECT to refuse rather than capture in that state, corroborated by TestAssistantHTTPE2E_HighBandUncitedRefusesHonestly PASSING with error_cause="provider_unavailable". report.md#simplify-phase. Verdict ONE_FINDING_FIXED. Reviewed the only code file this packet changed; six candidate findings were checked against the package and REJECTED as non-defects rather than turned into churn. The one real finding was a claim-exceeds-evidence defect of the same shape this packet has already been corrected for three times: TestAssistantIntegration_BUG061006_BareShortcutPersistsNothing asserted only that no BLANK row landed, while its name and its own comment claimed coverage of a 'placeholder' persist -- so a wrong fix storing the /ask token verbatim would have passed the test while violating the property. Strengthened the predicate to also match the shortcut token and renamed the helper to stop the name overstating the query. report.md#stabilize-phase. Verdict STABLE, scoped deliberately to the surface this packet changed. The changed code is clean on all four axes, and its central property is structural rather than incidental: the duplicate acknowledgement was fixed by REMOVING A SINK, so there is no acknowledgement state for concurrent turns to race on -- which matters because the two ingresses are mutually exclusive and the webhook one is genuinely concurrent (one net/http goroutine per request into the same safeHandleMessage). No goroutine, timer, buffer, retry or config value was added; the request-size bound was preserved by moving truncation into the shared persistTextIdea rather than leaving it in handleTextCapture, and redelivery is idempotent via errDuplicate -> nil. ./smackerel.sh lint (the go vet surface) exit 0. HONEST LIMIT: no race detector was run -- the repo CLI has no --race selector and a bare 'go test -race' would violate terminal discipline, so the concurrency verdict is static (field-mutability + go vet), not a dynamic-detector claim. THE VERDICT IS SCOPED ON PURPOSE: two real defects were found NEXT TO the changed code -- webhook mode never closing b.done, so shutdown abandons Bot.Stop before the assembler flush and buffered captures can be lost; and the facade counting outcome=captured before the capture hook has run, so a persist failure is invisible to metrics. Neither was introduced by this fix, neither is inside its three-file surface, and both are recorded as observations with owners rather than folded into this packet's verdict: marking this packet UNSTABLE on their account would misroute a fix cycle onto code that is not at fault, while leaving them unrecorded would waste the one review that found them. A third observation (local dev-stack container with networks=0 crash-looping against 'postgres') is environment drift, was verified read-only, and was deliberately NOT repaired because other suites may be using Docker. Nothing was fixed inline, no DoD item was checked, scopes.md and uservalidation.md were not touched, and certification.certifiedCompletedPhases was deliberately NOT written: bubbles.stabilize is diagnostic with no certifying authority and bubbles.validate has still not run.

WEBHOOK-SHUTDOWN-FLUSH (owner bubbles.plan; found by the stabilize phase, see report.md#stabilize-obs-1): in webhook mode nothing ever closes b.done — close(b.done) exists only inside the long-poll goroutine (bot.go:381) that wiring.go:845-847 deliberately does not start — so Bot.Stop always burns its 5s wait (bot.go:1562-1566) while shutdown budgets it 2s and ABANDONS it without cancelling (shutdown.go:87-91 with runWithTimeout at :159-183). assembler.FlushAll/mediaAssembler.FlushAll therefore race process exit instead of running inside the shutdown budget, so buffered conversation/media captures can be lost on restart. Pre-existing since spec 061 SCOPE-05; NOT introduced by BUG-061-006 and outside its three-file fix surface. Latent today because the recorded deploy evidence indicates long_poll; it fires the day the transport is switched to webhook, which is when it would be hardest to attribute. Repair (close b.done at construction when the goroutine will not run, or make Stop mode-aware) is a shutdown-semantics decision for the spec 061 SCOPE-05 owner.

CAPTURE-FAILURE-UNOBSERVABLE (owner bubbles.plan; found by the stabilize phase, see report.md#stabilize-obs-2): the facade emits FacadeTurnsTotal and the assistant_turn log line from a defer inside Handle (facade.go:511-513, :559), with deriveFacadeOutcome returning OutcomeCaptured for CaptureRoute (facade.go:1891-1893) — all BEFORE the transport's capture hook runs (adapter.go:390). A capture-persist failure is therefore counted outcome=captured / status=saved_as_idea, and honestCaptureFallbackFailure does not revise it (it sets StatusAnswered and leaves ErrorCause empty). BUG-061-006 strictly improved this — before it CaptureFn had no error return at all, and the fix added the error channel plus slog.Error at bot.go:821 — but did not close it: the prose the user sees is honest while the structured signal is not, which is in tension with the repo's own invariant that refusal-vs-answer distinguishability is structural (Status/ErrorCause), not prose. Closing it means either a dedicated counter on the capture-fallback path or moving outcome emission after the transport capture hook; both are design changes outside this packet.
